fields.text: Can a spoken poem KEEP ITS FORM? A GLM director picks one poem spec from a menu printed in its own prompt (four themes; every spec is scheme AABB with exactly 8 syllables per line and four carded line-ending words - the two rhyme pairs spelled out) and copies out a POEM CARD. A GLM poet writes exactly four lines on the theme, each exactly 8 syllables, each ending with its carded word. MiniMax Speech reads the poem aloud. Whisper transcribes the audio blind - it never saw the poem. A GLM auditor scores two channels: FORM (the written poem against the card: end words in place, syllables counted line by line) and EAR (the transcript against the poem: the four end words heard in order, words kept through the voice). A Decide judge headlines round 1. That verdict is not the deliverable: a GLM editor rewrites only the failing lines (gated - on a perfect audit it must reproduce the poem verbatim), MiniMax Speech re-reads the corrected poem, Whisper re-transcribes it, and the same auditor re-scores both channels. The corrected spoken poem is the flow's final output.
A four-line spoken poem for a children's poetry corner, about a lighthouse keeper's cat who watches the harbour at night.

fields.system:
You are a poetry editor. Given a POEM SETTING, design a POEM CARD for one four-line spoken poem. Choose ONE spec from this menu ONLY, and copy its spec EXACTLY - the theme, the scheme, the meter and all four end words:

MENU:
1. LIGHTHOUSE CAT - THEME: a lighthouse keeper's cat watching the harbour at night. END WORDS: line 1 light, line 2 night, line 3 sea, line 4 free.
2. MARKET GARDENER - THEME: a gardener planting seeds after spring rain. END WORDS: line 1 rain, line 2 grain, line 3 sun, line 4 run.
3. LITTLE TRAIN - THEME: a small train climbing to a hill town at dawn. END WORDS: line 1 track, line 2 back, line 3 hill, line 4 still.
4. WINTER FOX - THEME: a fox crossing a snowy wood at dusk. END WORDS: line 1 snow, line 2 glow, line 3 pine, line 4 shine.

Every spec uses SCHEME: AABB (line 1 rhymes with line 2, line 3 rhymes with line 4 - the end words above are the rhyme pairs) and METER: exactly 8 syllables in every line.

Output ONLY the card, in exactly this format, copying the chosen spec without changing any of it:
POEM: <the spec name>
THEME: <the theme>
SCHEME: AABB
METER: 8 syllables every line
END WORDS: 1 <word> / 2 <word> / 3 <word> / 4 <word>
LINE COUNT: 4
No other text.

fields.system:
You are a poetry-form auditor. The input gives a POEM CARD (POEM name, THEME, SCHEME: AABB, METER: 8 syllables every line, END WORDS for lines 1-4), then the POEM as written (exactly the four lines the poet produced), then a TRANSCRIPT - what a blind listener model heard when the poem was read aloud; it never saw the poem. Score in exactly this format:
END WORDS: <number of the poem's 4 lines whose last word is exactly the card's end word for that line, ignoring capitalisation> of 4
METER: <number of the poem's 4 lines that have exactly 8 syllables> of 4
METER DETAIL: L1 <count> / L2 <count> / L3 <count> / L4 <count>
HEARD END WORDS: <number of the card's 4 end words that appear in the transcript in card order, as whole words, ignoring capitalisation and punctuation> of 4
WORDS KEPT: <number of the poem's words that the transcript carries in the same order with the same value - a number heard as words counts as kept> of <the poem's total word count>
SUMMARY: <one short line naming what held and what failed, and on which channel - FORM for the written poem, EAR for the hearing>
Count syllables carefully, word by word: a syllable is one vowel sound, a silent final e adds none, and -ed adds a syllable only when it sounds as its own beat. Score strictly from the texts given. A rhyme is in place only when the end words are the card's words - near rhymes do not count.

nodes.name: Form audit - GLM scores end words, meter and what the ear kept

fields.question: The poem should be a four-line poem on the card's theme in AABB form: line 1 ends with the card's first end word, line 2 with its rhyming pair, line 3 with the third end word and line 4 with its rhyming pair, and every line has exactly 8 syllables. The audit in the text scores the written poem's form against the card and what a blind transcription heard of the spoken reading. Choose the one label that best fits the round-1 poem.
fields.options:
rhymes true
rhyme slipped
meter broke
voice garbled it
not a poem
